history.dynasty: Phulkian (Patiala state); founded by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh (reign 1900–1938)
history.period: Built 1936 — Wikipedia's infobox lists 'Completed 1938', a conflict flagged below
history.summary: The Shri Kali Devi Mandir on Mall Road, opposite the Baradari Gardens, is Patiala's premier Hindu temple. It was built in 1936 by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala (reigned 1900–1938), who, inspired by the Kali temples of Bengal, transported a six-foot-tall black stone statue of Maa Kali and the sacred Paawan Jyot (eternal flame) from Bengal to Patiala — a logistical feat of the pre-independence era — and offered the first bali (sacrifice) of a water buffalo at the temple. Its architecture blends traditional Indian styles with intricate carvings and murals depicting scenes from Hindu mythology, and its beauty led to it being declared a national monument. The complex also houses a much older temple of Shri Raj Rajeshwari Ji at its centre. Maa Kali here is the kul devi (family deity) of many families, and the temple attracts Hindu and Sikh devotees from distant places; Navratri brings huge crowds over nine days. Offerings include mustard oil, daal (lentils), sweets, coconuts, bangles and chunnis — and also goats, hens and liquor, which goes into a 'Sharab Kund' on the premises (the temple's own site says over 60,000 liquor bottles are offered during Navratras alone). CSV town Patiala is correct; district Patiala. CONFLICT FLAG: Wikipedia's infobox gives 'Completed 1938' while the article text and all other sources (the temple's official site, Bharat Temples, Vibhaga) say the temple was built/founded in 1936; treat 1936 as the primary date with the caveat.

name: Shri Kali Devi Mandir
town_description: Patiala was the capital of the Phulkian princely state founded by Baba Ala Singh in 1763 and remains a cultural centre of Punjab. The Kali Devi Temple stands opposite the Baradari Gardens on Mall Road, one of the city's landmark religious sites.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, the nearest major airport (~65 km, verify).
travel.railway: Patiala Railway Station (~3 km, verify); autos and taxis to Mall Road / Baradari Gardens.
travel.road: On Mall Road opposite the Baradari Gardens; easily reached by auto or taxi within Patiala city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Navratri for the major nine-day celebrations (very crowded).
